title: Microburst-to-steady-state-cost-bridge
content:
Purpose
This is a working journal and lightweight model spec to bridge two operational regimes we frequently treat separately: short, high-amplitude microbursts (sub-second to tens-of-seconds arrival spikes) and the steady-state continuous stream we optimize for with batching/concurrency policies. Goal is to produce a spreadsheet-ready cost/latency transformation that product engineering and SRE can use to: (1) estimate incremental infra cost of microburst tolerance, (2) choose concurrency/batching knobs per-route, and (3) propose fallback sizing (hot standby pools, short-term scale-up policies).

Context and why this doc: 
- Many existing notes focus on continuous batching heuristics. Microbursts change the queueing boundary conditions: they reduce effective batching window and inflate p95 because of transient cold starts and admission throttling.
- We need a small, auditable model (spreadsheet) that maps: arrival shape + policy -> throughput, p95 estimate, token cost, and cold-start penalty.
- This doc documents assumptions, math, example scenarios, and concrete optimization recommendations.

Key definitions (how I use terms here):
- Microburst: a spike where instantaneous request rate > 5x baseline sustained for 1–60s.
- Steady-state: background arrival process approximated as Poisson with mean lambda0 and small variance over minutes.
- Admission window (W): conservative batching window in ms that the scheduler uses before dispatching a batch.
- Concurrency cap (C): number of simultaneous in-flight model slots per instance.
- Hot fraction (H): proportion of pool kept warm (no cold-start) to service microburst without spin-up.

Assumptions (spreadsheet friendly)
- Service time per request depends on prompt length and generated tokens. Use per-token model: base_setup_ms + gen_ms_per_token * expected_tokens. Example numbers used below are placeholders for x86 A100-like hosts.
- Kernel saturation: throughput per slot degrades when batch size < optimal_batch due to GPU utilization; we model this as a mild nonlinear taper: eff_factor(batch) = 0.6 + 0.4 * min(batch, optimal_batch)/optimal_batch.
- Cold start penalty: a slot that was idle and must be scheduled costs extra 1200 ms (spin-up + model load) for private deployments, 400–800 ms for hosted prewarmed pools.
- Queueing discipline approximated with M/G/c with time-varying lambda(t) (piecewise constant for spike periods). We approximate p95 with an empirical interpolation between M/M/c heavy-traffic asymptote and observed batch-penalty dominated regime.

Model structure (how to lay out the spreadsheet)
- Sheet "scenario_inputs": one row per scenario with columns: scenario_name, baseline_rps, burst_peak_rps, burst_duration_s, avg_prompt_tokens, base_setup_ms, gen_ms_per_token, W_ms, C_per_instance, instances_provisioned, hot_fraction, cost_per_instance_hour_usd.
- Sheet "util_and_batch": computed columns per scenario: lambda_eff = instantaneous_rps; expected_batch = max(1, lambda_eff * (W_ms/1000.0)); eff_factor; per-request_service_ms = base_setup_ms/expected_batch + gen_ms_per_token*avg_prompt_tokens; slot_throughput_rps = 1000.0 / per-request_service_ms * expected_batch * eff_factor; capacity_rps = instances_provisioned * C_per_instance * slot_throughput_rps.
- Sheet "latency_estimates": compute queueing_p95_ms using piecewise rule below, add cold_start_fraction = max(0, 1 - hot_fraction - (lambda_eff / (instances_provisioned * C_per_instance * slot_throughput_rps))). ColdStart_penalty_ms = cold_start_fraction * cold_start_ms_estimate. Total_p95_ms = queueing_p95_ms + ColdStart_penalty_ms.

Piecewise p95 rule (spreadsheet formula outline)
- If lambda_eff < 0.6 * capacity_rps: p95 ~= service_ms * (1 + 0.25*(util)) where util = lambda_eff / capacity_rps. (Regime: plenty of headroom, batching dominates)
- If 0.6 <= util <= 0.95: interpolate with Erlang C approximation adjusted for batch inefficiency (use simpler form to keep sheet fast): p95 ~= service_ms * (1 + 1.5*(util/(1-util))).
- If util > 0.95: p95 grows superlinearly; p95 ~= service_ms * (1 + 6*(util/(1-util))). Also trigger alert indicator and compute required extra instances to bring util to 0.7.

Example scenario (cells included so people can paste)
- scenario_inputs!A2 = "checkout-burst-1"
- scenario_inputs!B2 = 10          // baseline_rps
- scenario_inputs!C2 = 200         // burst_peak_rps
- scenario_inputs!D2 = 12          // burst_duration_s
- scenario_inputs!E2 = 40          // avg_prompt_tokens
- scenario_inputs!F2 = 12          // base_setup_ms
- scenario_inputs!G2 = 3           // gen_ms_per_token
- scenario_inputs!H2 = 30          // W_ms (batch window)
- scenario_inputs!I2 = 2           // C_per_instance
- scenario_inputs!J2 = 20          // instances_provisioned
- scenario_inputs!K2 = 0.6         // hot_fraction
- scenario_inputs!L2 = 4.5         // cost_per_instance_hour_usd

Manual worked numbers (paste into sheet to validate):
- expected_batch_at_peak = min(1, 200 * 0.03) = 6 (30 ms window -> 0.03 s)
- eff_factor = 0.6 + 0.4*(6/16) = 0.6 + 0.15 = 0.75 (assuming optimal_batch=16)
- per_request_service_ms = 12/6 + 3*40 = 2 + 120 = 122 ms
- slot_throughput_rps ~= 1000/122 * 6 * 0.75 = 8.1967 * 4.5 = 36.885 rps per slot
- capacity_rps = 20 * 2 * 36.885 = 1475.4 rps (so burst fits without scaling)
- util_at_peak = 200 / 1475.4 = 0.135 -> p95 approx = 122 * (1 + 0.25*0.135) = 126.1 ms
- cold_start_fraction = max(0, 1-0.6 - (200 / 1475.4)) = max(0, 0.4 - 0.135) = 0.265 -> ColdStart_penalty_ms = 0.265 * 1200 = 318 ms
- total_p95 ~= 126 + 318 = 444 ms (shows cold-start dominates p95 despite capacity headroom)

Interpretation of example:
- Even though raw compute capacity can handle the burst, cold-start exposure (hot_fraction=0.6) increases p95 a lot. For this route, increasing hot_fraction to 0.9 or reducing cold_start_ms (pre-warmed containers) is more cost effective than adding instances.

Optimization heuristics and recommendations (actionable rules to encode into Optimize):
1) Hot-first knob: keep hot_fraction >= min(0.95, burst_peak_rps / (instances_provisioned * C_per_instance * slot_throughput_rps * 0.25)) for routes with burstiness > 5x baseline. This is cheaper than scaling if bursts are short (< 60s).
2) Window tuning: reduce W_ms in microburst-prone routes to bias towards lower cold-start fraction by letting more immediate dispatch; but watch batch size drop and eff_factor fall. Suggest parameter sweep: 10, 20, 30, 50 ms in sheet and plot cost vs p95.
3) Fallback scaling: if predicted p95 > SLA threshold (e.g., 500 ms) for expected burst duration, evaluate short-lived scale-up of instances_provisioned for the burst window only. Compute break-even: extra_cost = delta_instances * cost_per_instance_hour * (burst_duration_s/3600) vs. SLA-penalty metric or SLO budget.
4) Pre-warm vs keep-alive tradeoff: pre-warmed slots increase hot_fraction but cost hours even without traffic. Use the sheet to compute amortized prewarm cost per expected burst per day (prewarm_hours/day * cost / bursts_per_day). If bursts/day < 3 and duration < 30s, prewarm usually loses to on-demand scale.

Spreadsheet visualizations to add:
- heatmap: surge_peak_rps vs base_rps with cells colored by min_p95 and min_cost strategy (prewarm, scale, throttle).
- scenario waterfall: baseline p95 -> add queueing penalty -> add cold-start penalty -> add spin-up recovery -> final p95.
- sensitivity spider chart: varying W_ms, hot_fraction, instances by +/- 50%.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self and collaborators):
- Validate cold_start_ms numbers across Private vs Hosted (Omar to run microbench).
- Need a small dataset of real arrival traces for 10 customers to fit the util->p95 interpolation better (Rita to pull traces and anonymize).
- Should we model queueing as stateful across bursts (i.e., residual KV cache warmness) or treat bursts as independent? I suspect stateful effects reduce cold-start fraction for repeated bursts within 10 minutes.
- Hook the sheet to an Optimize experiment runner: output recommended knob set and expected delta cost and p95. Connect to github pr for UI: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/452.

Quick checklist before handing to SRE:
- [ ] Convert the piecewise p95 formulas into sheet-safe formulas (avoid iterative loops).
- [ ] Add a baseline scenario set for top 8 customer routes.
- [ ] Add cost tradeoff heatmap for prewarm vs scale.
- [ ] Run small canary test with hot_fraction=0.9 for checkout route for 48h and compare p95.

References and notes:
- Related Linear ticket: RI-4387 (microburst analysis).
- Past experiments: see serving-runtime/mini-batch-sla-surface-sketch.json and microburst-reservoir-batching-explainer-wip (these have overlapping numbers but not the prewarm-cost bridge perspective).

Contact and next steps:
- Ping in #serving-runtime and add this sheet to the design review thread.
- I will build the initial sheet and upload to shared drive as microburst_cost_bridge_v0.ods and link back here.

Signed-off: Maya Chen (notes), Ethan Park (math review), Rita Alvarez (data), Omar Singh (bench)

End of doc
